title: Associations between the use of social media and AI chatbots, basic psychological needs, and mental health among adolescents
summary:
This study examines how adolescents use social media and AI chatbots and how this relates to subjective well-being. In recent years, digital media have become an integral part of young people’s everyday lives. However, the effects of this usage on mental health remain largely unclear. A particular focus is placed on how basic psychological needs for autonomy, relatedness, and competence are experienced in daily life as well as in the context of using artificial intelligence. The study investigates whether these needs are rather satisfied or frustrated by digital services and how this is associated with well-being and psychological distress.

The study will survey students aged 13–18 at schools in the Aachen region and surrounding areas. Participation is voluntary and requires written informed consent (for minors, from legal guardians) at the respective schools. Participants will complete a single anonymous online questionnaire during school time, administered via the SoSci Survey platform, which takes approximately 30 minutes. The questionnaire includes items on digital media use as well as on personal experiences and well-being.
conditions: No specific disease; investigation of mental health and media use in healthy adolescents
